description: Design system regulations for Android applications based on Material Design 3 guidelines, Google Play requirements, and WCAG accessibility standards.

references.name: Material Design 3
references.description: Google's open-source design system for building beautiful, usable products.

references.name: WCAG 2.1
references.description: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines used as baseline for mobile accessibility.

references.name: Google Play Design Guidelines
references.description: Quality guidelines for apps distributed on Google Play.

regulations.title: Type Scale Compliance
regulations.description: All text elements must follow the Material Design 3 type scale to ensure consistent, readable typography across the application.

rules.requirement: Body text must be at least 14sp to ensure readability on all device sizes.
rules.rationale: Text below 14sp becomes difficult to read on standard mobile screens.

rules.requirement: Applications must use a clear type hierarchy with distinct sizes for display, headline, title, body, and label roles.
rules.rationale: A well-defined type hierarchy helps users scan and understand content structure.

rules.requirement: All text must support user-configured font scaling up to 200% without content being clipped or overlapping.
rules.rationale: Users with low vision rely on system font scaling to read content.

rules.requirement: Text sizes must be specified in sp (scale-independent pixels) rather than dp or px to respect user font size preferences.
rules.rationale: The sp unit scales with user accessibility settings while dp and px do not.

regulations.title: Color System and Theming
regulations.description: Applications must implement a robust color system using Material Design 3 dynamic color and token-based theming.

rules.requirement: Normal text must have a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 against its background. Large text (18sp+ or 14sp+ bold) must have at least 3:1.
rules.rationale: WCAG 2.1 Level AA requires these minimum contrast ratios for readable text.

rules.requirement: Applications must provide a dark theme that respects system-level dark mode settings and uses appropriate surface and on-surface colors.
rules.rationale: Dark themes reduce eye strain, save battery on OLED displays, and are expected by users.

rules.requirement: Color must not be the only means of conveying information. Additional visual cues such as icons, patterns, or text labels must accompany color-coded elements.
rules.rationale: Approximately 8% of men and 0.5% of women have color vision deficiency.

rules.requirement: Applications targeting Android 12+ should support Material You dynamic color to harmonize with the user's wallpaper and theme.
rules.rationale: Dynamic color creates a personalized experience and visual consistency across the OS.

regulations.title: Spacing and Layout Grid
regulations.description: Layout and spacing must follow Material Design's 8dp grid system to maintain visual rhythm and consistency.

rules.requirement: All spacing values (margins, padding, gaps) must be multiples of 8dp. Small elements may use 4dp for tighter spacing.
rules.rationale: An 8dp grid creates consistent spatial relationships and aligns with screen pixel densities.

rules.requirement: Interactive elements must have a minimum touch target size of 48x48dp.
rules.rationale: Touch targets smaller than 48dp cause user frustration and accessibility failures.

rules.requirement: Content must maintain at least 16dp horizontal margins from the screen edges on mobile devices.
rules.rationale: Adequate margins prevent accidental edge interactions and improve readability.

rules.requirement: Layouts must adapt across compact (<600dp), medium (600-840dp), and expanded (>840dp) width breakpoints.
rules.rationale: Android devices range from phones to tablets to foldables and need responsive layouts.

regulations.title: Accessibility Requirements
regulations.description: Applications must meet WCAG 2.1 Level AA and Android-specific accessibility requirements to be usable by all people.

rules.requirement: All meaningful images and icons must have contentDescription attributes. Decorative images must have contentDescription set to null.
rules.rationale: Screen readers (TalkBack) rely on content descriptions to convey non-text elements.

rules.requirement: Interactive elements must have a logical focus traversal order that follows the visual reading flow of the screen.
rules.rationale: Keyboard and switch device users navigate sequentially and need a predictable order.

rules.requirement: Changes in UI state (loading, errors, success) must be announced to accessibility services using live regions or announcements.
rules.rationale: Users relying on screen readers cannot see visual state changes.

rules.requirement: Adjacent touch targets must have at least 8dp of spacing between them to prevent mis-taps.
rules.rationale: Closely spaced targets are difficult for users with motor impairments.

regulations.title: Component Usage Standards
regulations.description: UI components must follow Material Design 3 component specifications for consistent behavior and appearance.

rules.requirement: Screens should use a clear button hierarchy: one filled button for the primary action, tonal or outlined buttons for secondary actions, and text buttons for tertiary actions.
rules.rationale: A clear visual hierarchy helps users identify the most important action quickly.

rules.requirement: Applications must use standard navigation components (Navigation Bar, Navigation Rail, Navigation Drawer) appropriate for the device form factor.
rules.rationale: Familiar navigation patterns reduce cognitive load and learning time.

rules.requirement: Dialogs must be used sparingly for critical decisions and should include a clear title, body, and action buttons. Dialogs must be dismissible.
rules.rationale: Overuse of dialogs interrupts workflow and fatigues users.

rules.requirement: Operations taking longer than 1 second must display a loading indicator. Operations taking longer than 10 seconds should show a progress bar with percentage or determinate progress.
rules.rationale: Users need feedback that the system is working to prevent repeated taps or abandonment.

regulations.title: Navigation Architecture
regulations.description: Applications must implement predictable, consistent navigation that follows Android platform conventions.

rules.requirement: The system back button/gesture must behave predictably: closing dialogs, popping the back stack, or exiting the application. Custom back behavior must be communicated clearly.
rules.rationale: Inconsistent back behavior is a top source of user confusion on Android.

rules.requirement: Key application destinations must support deep linking to allow direct access from notifications, widgets, and external links.
rules.rationale: Deep linking improves discoverability and integration with the Android ecosystem.

rules.requirement: Navigation state must be preserved across configuration changes (rotation, resizing) and process death.
rules.rationale: Users lose trust in applications that reset their position unexpectedly.

regulations.title: Motion and Animation
regulations.description: Animations and transitions must enhance usability while respecting user motion preferences.

rules.requirement: Applications must respect the system 'Remove Animations' accessibility setting by disabling or reducing non-essential animations.
rules.rationale: Animations can cause discomfort for users with vestibular disorders.

rules.requirement: UI transitions should be between 200ms and 500ms. Transitions shorter than 100ms feel abrupt; transitions longer than 700ms feel sluggish.
rules.rationale: Appropriate duration ensures users can follow the transition without feeling delayed.

rules.requirement: Every animation must serve a functional purpose: guiding attention, showing spatial relationships, or providing feedback. Purely decorative loops are discouraged.
rules.rationale: Gratuitous animation wastes battery, distracts users, and hurts performance.

regulations.title: Icon Standards
regulations.description: Icons must follow Material Design icon guidelines for clarity and consistency.

rules.requirement: System icons must be 24dp in size within a 48dp touch target area. Smaller icons (20dp, 18dp) may be used in dense contexts like toolbars.
rules.rationale: Consistent icon sizing creates visual harmony and meets touch target requirements.

rules.requirement: Icons used for primary navigation or actions must include a text label. Icon-only buttons are acceptable only for universally recognized actions (close, back, search).
rules.rationale: Icons without labels are frequently misinterpreted, especially across cultures.

rules.requirement: Application launcher icons must be provided as adaptive icons with separate foreground and background layers.
rules.rationale: Adaptive icons ensure the app icon renders correctly across different device shapes and launchers.

regulations.title: User Feedback Patterns
regulations.description: Applications must provide clear, timely feedback for user actions and system events.

rules.requirement: Error messages must be human-readable, describe what went wrong, and suggest a corrective action when possible. Generic messages like 'Error occurred' are prohibited.
rules.rationale: Clear error messages reduce user frustration and support requests.

rules.requirement: Snackbars must be displayed for at least 4 seconds and no more than 10 seconds. Snackbars with actions must remain until dismissed or acted upon.
rules.rationale: Too-short snackbars are missed; too-long snackbars occlude content.

rules.requirement: Critical actions (delete, submit, error) should provide haptic feedback using the system haptic API when haptics are enabled.
rules.rationale: Haptic feedback reinforces actions for users who may not be looking at the screen.

regulations.title: Privacy and Data Display
regulations.description: Applications must handle user data display in accordance with privacy best practices and platform policies.

rules.requirement: Sensitive data (passwords, payment info, personal identifiers) must be masked by default with an option to reveal temporarily.
rules.rationale: Visible sensitive data can be inadvertently exposed through screen sharing or shoulder surfing.

rules.requirement: Before requesting a runtime permission, the application must display a UI explaining why the permission is needed and how it will be used.
rules.rationale: Users are more likely to grant permissions when they understand the purpose.

rules.requirement: Screens displaying sensitive information must set FLAG_SECURE to prevent screenshots and screen recording in secure contexts.
rules.rationale: FLAG_SECURE prevents data leakage through screenshots and recent apps preview.
